text:
alex: Heads-up — saw TP all-reduce latency regression on small-chunk workload (kv-cache flush bursts). Profiling attached below.

maya: Hmm, which run? staging or canary?

alex: staging, gpu pool tp-16x, commit abc123. trace: https://ci/internal/trace/2845

cheng: Can you paste the ncu timeline? do we see long gaps between send/recv calls?

alex: Copying minimal profiler dump:

```txt
nccl_allreduce_start -> 10us
ncclSend -> 40us
ncclRecv -> 1500us
allreduce_total -> 2.1ms
expected ~0.6ms
CPU wait time -> 1.1ms
```

sam: Looks like handshake/ack latency dominating for small messages. Kernel selector might pick ring which requires more hops.

maya: Did kernel autoselect recently change? I thought we had kernel-gate for msgsize < 4KB.

devon: We did a heuristic tweak last week: we lowered tree threshold to 2KB to optimize for bigger batches. Might regress tiny-message perf.

cheng: Also KV cache generates many small KV flushes (~512B chunks) which interact badly with NCCL rendezvous. We should try batching at RPC layer.

alex: Reproduced with microbenchmark: allreduce of 512B across TP 8 nodes. Results:

```bash
for i in {1..100}; do measure_allreduce 512; done | awk '{sum+=$1} END{print sum/NR}'
# avg = 2.05ms
```

sam: If ring path includes extra handshakes per hop, message-size cliff causes superlinear overhead. Tree algorithm reduces hops for small messages.

maya: Could we force tree for <4KB in runtime and run A/B? Would also affect larger runs.

devon: Quick patch idea: add adaptive windowing — aggregate small KV flushes into batch until either size>2KB or latency budget reached. That reduces number of allreduce calls.

alex: Filed perf job: https://ci/internal/job/2845-run with both patches: kernel-force-tree and adaptive-windowing. infra-bot queued the experiments.

infra-bot: Job 2845-run queued on cluster 'staging-tp'. ETA 12m.

cheng: Also instrument NCCL rendezvous: add per-call handshake time metric. If handshake>300us, early abort to tree fallback.

sam: Good. Also check overlap: current schedule seems to stall compute until allreduce completes for small msgs. Maybe we can issue async sends and continue compute.

maya: Agree — add comm/compute overlap metrics to console per-route.

alex: Thanks all — will monitor jobs and post results. :eyes:
